name: True Grit

approach_variants.name: Sunrise Mine Trail #707, Headlee Pass, Vesper-Wolf saddle
approach_variants.notes:
Sunrise Mine trailhead off the Mountain Loop Highway via Sunrise Mine Road (FR 4065). Trail #707 crosses the South Fork Stillaguamish on a log almost immediately — a real obstacle in high runoff — then climbs through Wirtz Basin, breaks into cairned talus and boulder fields, and reaches Headlee Pass at about 4,720 ft and 2.7 miles. The pass is a narrow rocky notch with loose footing where rockfall from above is a genuine hazard.

Past the pass the trail drops briefly through trees, crosses about a third of a mile of talus to Vesper Creek and follows it up to Vesper Lake (Lake Elan) at about 4,950 ft, 3.5 miles and 2,700 ft from the car — last reliable water.

Stay on the ordinary Vesper summit trail up talus and slabs to roughly 5,600-5,700 ft, then leave it and swing north across the slabs. Three hours or more car to base.
approach_variants.season: Jul-Sep; earlier needs axe and crampons for the ledge traverse
hazards: Rockfall in the Headlee Pass couloir
Steep exposed heather benches, slick when wet
Snow on the ledge traverse into early-to-mid summer
Loose rock on the face — treat as alpine despite the bolted belays
approach_variants.baseFinding:
Aim for the two large cairns on the saddle at about 5,700 ft (near 48.01375 -121.51451), with Copper Lake below to the northwest; the heather ledge system starts about 30 ft above the cairns on third-class slabs, not from the saddle floor. Traverse east on the goat trail through the heather.

True Grit itself is identified by its first anchor, not by its first moves. Pitch 1 is about 200 ft of easy, clean granite and finishes by stepping left to a bolted belay sitting directly beneath an obvious narrow chimney. If there is no chimney above the anchor you have reached, you are not on True Grit. It is the more direct of the two lines here — Ragged Edge jogs sharply right in its first pitch or two, so a line that keeps going straight up is this one.

approach: Start at the Sunrise Mine Trailhead (Sunrise Mine Trail #707) off the Mountain Loop Highway near Big Four/Barlow Pass. The trail begins in second-growth forest and almost immediately crosses the South Fork Stillaguamish via a log crossing that can be a genuine obstacle during high runoff (early season/after rain). From there the trail climbs steadily through Wirtz Basin, breaks out of the trees into open talus and boulder fields marked by cairns, and reaches Headlee Pass at roughly 4,720 ft and 2.7 miles in — a narrow, rocky notch/couloir with loose rock underfoot where rockfall from parties above is a real hazard. Past the pass the trail drops briefly through trees, then crosses about a third of a mile of talus to Vesper Creek, which it follows up to Vesper Lake (Lake Elan, ~4,950 ft, ~3.5 mi/~2,700 ft gain from the trailhead) — the last reliable running water before the climb. From the lake, cross the outlet and follow the obvious talus ridgeline up to the saddle/col between Vesper and Wolf Peak. From the saddle, a ledge system cuts across Vesper's north face at roughly 5,800 ft, reached by walking out steep, exposed heather benches that get slick when wet and hold a steep snow slope into early-to-mid summer (ice axe and possibly crampons recommended for that window). The ledge leads to a small notch overlooking the Vesper Glacier remnant, near where True Grit's start is found. Allow 3+ hours from the trailhead to the base of the route.

waypoints.name: Sunrise Mine Trailhead
waypoints.note: End of Forest Road 4065; follow Sunrise Mine Trail to Headlee Pass then around Sperry Peak to the Vesper/Sperry basin.
waypoints.directions: From Granite Falls, drive the Mountain Loop Highway east about 27 to 28 miles, then turn onto Sunrise Mine Road, Forest Road 4065. Follow roughly 2.3 to 2.5 miles of gravel to the road's end at the Sunrise Mine Trailhead, around 2,400 ft, where Trail No. 707 starts. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

waypoints.name: Cairned pass toward Copper Lake / start of ledge traverse
waypoints.directions: Take Sunrise Mine Trail No. 707 across the unbridged South Fork Stillaguamish, up Wirtz Basin and the loose, narrow couloir to Headlee Pass at about 4,720 ft, 2.7 miles in. Beyond, drop briefly, cross talus to Vesper Creek and follow it to Vesper Lake at about 4,950 ft, the last reliable water, then climb talus and slabs to the two large cairns on the saddle at about 5,700 ft, with Copper Lake below to the northwest.

waypoints.name: North Face ledge-access notch (True Grit start)
waypoints.directions: Climb third-class slabs about 30 ft above the cairns onto the heather ledge system of the north face and follow the goat trail across the ledges to the start. Expect steep snow on the ledges into early-to-mid summer. The first pitch ends at a bolted belay directly beneath an obvious narrow chimney; with no chimney above, you are not on the route.

waypoints.name: Vesper Peak north face
waypoints.note: True Grit is a 5-pitch, 5.8 line up the north face, one of the original moderate routes on the wall.
waypoints.directions: Climb five pitches: easy granite to the bolted belay under the chimney, the chimney or the corner to its right, slab and a small overhang to a cramped stance, the long finger-to-hand splitter crack, and an easy finishing pitch to the top of the headwall.

days.note: A clean, popular 5-pitch granite line on excellent rock, done as a long day from the Sunrise Mine Trailhead. Approach mirrors the other North Face routes via Headlee Pass and Vesper Lake; descent is the Class 2 south/west talus walk-off back to the lake.
days.title: True Grit, car to car

schedule.label: Top out
schedule.detail: 5 pitches, 5.8, exposed and scenic upper face.

schedule.label: Descend
schedule.detail: Class 2 south/west talus gully to Vesper Lake.

days.objective: Climb True Grit (5.8, 5 pitches) on Vesper's North Face

itinerary.totalNote: A long single day car-to-car: ~10-11 hrs, ~4,400 ft gain, 5 pitches of clean 5.8 granite.
